methodologyNote: Authoritative sweep run against an isolated next dev instance (port 3101, distDir=.next-pt01-audit via a temporary PT01_DIST_DIR override in next.config.mjs, reverted after this run) rather than the shared localhost:3000 dev server. The shared server was confirmed, via direct filesystem check, to have a persistently missing client hydration bundle (.next/static/chunks/main-app.js absent since before this session started, not regenerating despite hundreds of requests) caused by a concurrent, unrelated next build process (PID 112940, still running after 55+ minutes) writing to the same .next/ directory next dev reads from -- both processes share the default distDir with no isolation. An initial sweep against the shared server (see render-pass-run.log for the full transcript) found 12 failing routes, all bearing one of two build-contention signatures (a server-side "Cannot find module .../vendor-chunks/..." webpack error, or repeated 404s on core _next/static/ chunks); a further check against a broader set of loading-state routes found the contamination had worsened over time and was affecting a still-larger, growing set of routes. This is the same multi-worktree .next contention failure mode already documented in STANDING_DIRECTIVES.md (the next.config.mjs cpus:1 comment) and WGR-001. Switching to an isolated build-output directory fully resolved it -- the clean re-run below shows only 1 genuine failure (a real, reproducible application bug, not environmental) out of 146 routes.
